narrative.overview: The page is the product's own man page, printed on uncoated reference stock. It refuses the category's dark terminal-and-neon hero and equal-card grid; it makes the manual the marketing. The world is a technical reference sheet: ivory paper with faint horizontal laid lines, dense carbon ink, red rules and markers, and a rubber stamp that signs the issue. One variable family, Archivo, carries the whole hierarchy through width rather than font mixing: compressed heavy caps for the display and section ladder, normal-width roman for reading, monospace only for machine literals. No cards, no shadows, no rounded corners, no glow.
keyCharacteristics: The man-page ladder as the page's spine: an indented label rail on the left with red tick markers.
Uncoated reference stock with carbon ink and rubber-stamp red as the only accent.
One variable family, Archivo, width-stepped from 62% display to 100% text.
The install command is the SYNOPSIS; the capabilities are the FLAGS; providers are FILES.
No cards, no shadows, no glass, no glowing edges: every surface is flat paper separated by ruled ink.

rules.name: The Bold Is Literal Rule
rules.body: Bold monospace means a literal CLI token; roman bold means a document section or emphasis. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Red Is a Mark Rule
rules.body: Stamp red is a mark, a tick, a stamp, or an passed flag. It never sets a sentence.

rules.name: The Left Ladder Rule
rules.body: Every major block begins with its all-caps section label indented on the left rail, bounded by a vertical rule.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Depth is hairline rules and tone steps between paper and plate. Nothing floats; no shadow is permitted.

dos: Keep the section ladder intact: LABEL on the rail, content in the body.
Use stamp red (#bf2f1c) only for stamps, rules, ticks, passed flags, and the primary action.
Keep all interactive targets at least 44px tall.
Preserve the paper-grain tile as the tactile ground.
donts: Add rounded corners, cards, soft shadows, or glowing outlines.
Add floating badges or eyebrows above section headings.
